2027-03-15.title: Sixth Monday of the Great Fast
2027-03-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I have come as light into the world
2027-03-15.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). The last full week of the fast before Hosanna Sunday.
2027-03-15.verse: I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me should not remain in the darkness.
theo: The sixth week of the Great Fast opens with one of the warmest pages Paul ever wrote. He had been forced to leave Thessalonica after only a few weeks, and he worried that the young Church would not survive persecution. So he sent Timothy back, and Timothy has now returned with good news. Paul can hardly contain himself: “For we now live, if you continue to stand firm in the Lord. How can we thank God enough for you in return for all the joy that we feel before our God because of you?” The apostle's own life seems to depend on the faith of his people. Then he prays for them: “And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all, just as we abound in love for you. And may he so strengthen your hearts in holiness that you may be blameless before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints.” This is what every good pastor, catechist and parent feels. We do not live for ourselves; we live when those entrusted to us stand firm. In these last weeks of the fast many families are far apart: children studying in Bengaluru or Delhi, parents working in the Gulf, grandparents keeping the house at home. Paul's prayer can become our prayer for them: that the Lord will make love increase, and strengthen hearts in holiness, until we meet face to face.

The Gospel is the last public word of Jesus in the first half of John's Gospel. After this he will speak only to his disciples at the supper. “Then Jesus cried aloud”: he raises his voice, as if to be heard by everyone who will ever live. “Whoever believes in me believes not in me but in him who sent me. And whoever sees me sees him who sent me.” To look at Jesus is to see the Father. Then comes the reason he came: “I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me should not remain in the darkness.” He does not come to condemn: “for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.” And yet a word refused does not disappear; “on the last day the word that I have spoken will serve as judge.” The same light that saves also shows what we have chosen. The fast has been a slow walk out of the dark rooms of the heart into this light. In the Holy Qurbana the light is not only spoken but given, for the Word who speaks to us is the Bread who feeds us. As the week of the Passion draws near, Jesus still cries aloud to us: do not remain in the darkness.
outline: Ask: who lives because I stand firm?
Paul's joy at the faith of his people.
To see Jesus is to see the Father.
“I have come as light into the world.”
live: Each evening this week name one family member who lives far from home, and pray Paul's prayer for them.
Before Hosanna Sunday, bring one dark corner of your life to the sacrament of reconciliation.
2027-03-15.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, light of the world, you came not to judge us but to save us. Do not let us remain in the darkness. Make us increase and abound in love for one another and for all, and strengthen our hearts in holiness, so that we may stand firm in you and be blameless before the Father when you come with all your saints. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Word who cried aloud in the temple speaks to us again, and then gives himself as the Bread of life; whoever receives him receives the Father who sent him.

quick: Paul lives because his people stand firm in the Lord.
Jesus came as light into the world, to save and not to condemn.
The word we refuse becomes our judge on the last day.
2027-03-15.action: Pray by name today for a family member who lives far away.
2027-03-15.question: Where am I still choosing to remain in the darkness?

family.explain: Jesus said: I came into the world like a light, so that no one who believes in me has to stay in the dark. When we are afraid in the dark, we switch on a lamp. When we are sad, or have done something wrong, Jesus is the light we can run to.
family.intention: We pray for family members and friends who live far from home.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family lives far away? Let us pray for them by name tonight.”

illus: A mother in Thrissur kept a small oil lamp burning at the family prayer corner every evening of the fast, though her son had not called home from Dubai for two years after a quarrel. Her younger daughter asked why she bothered. “So that if he comes back, he will see that the light was never put out,” she said. On the Saturday before Hosanna Sunday the phone rang. He had gone to confession at a parish in Dubai, and the priest had told him to call his mother first.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, shine on us now as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: For we now live, if you continue to stand firm in the Lord (1 Thessalonians 3:8). Whose faith keeps me alive, and whom do I strengthen?
I have come as light into the world (John 12:46). What part of my life still stays in the dark?
I came not to judge the world, but to save the world (John 12:47). Do I see Jesus as a judge to fear or a Saviour to trust?
pm.resp: Lord, let us not remain in the darkness.
interc: For the Church, that she may shine with the light of Christ.
For pastors and catechists, that their people may stand firm in the faith.
For families separated by work and study.
For those who are afraid to come back to the light.
For our group, that we may abound in love for one another and for all.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as light into the world. Strengthen our hearts in holiness and make us abound in love, so that we may welcome him with joy when he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul had left the young Church in Thessalonica too soon, and he was afraid for them. When Timothy returns with news of their faith and love, Paul says: for we now live, if you continue to stand firm in the Lord (1 Thessalonians 3:8).

That is the heart of every parent, teacher and priest. We live when those we love stand firm. Paul prays that the Lord will make them increase and abound in love, and strengthen their hearts in holiness (1 Thessalonians 3:12–13). Let us pray the same for our children and for family members far from home.
In the Gospel Jesus cries aloud: I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me should not remain in the darkness (John 12:46). He did not come to judge but to save.
Yet the word we refuse will one day be our judge. Hosanna Sunday is near. Let us not remain in the darkness: let us bring what is hidden to the light of confession this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: I came like a light into the world. When it is dark we need a lamp. Tonight, when you see a light at the prayer corner, remember that Jesus is the light for your heart.

sub: Faith that keeps a pastor alive.
q: Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all, just as we abound in love for you.
points.apply: Write or call one person whose faith has strengthened yours, and thank them.

concl: Christ came as light, not to condemn but to save; his word is very near to us.
Those who stand firm in the Lord give life to others; let love increase and abound among us.
2027-03-15.resolve: This week, pray each evening by name for someone far away, and step into the light of confession before Hosanna Sunday.
